description: energy-floor gate at default silenceThreshold=0.005 -- a 30 Hz bass tone (raw i16 sine). amplitude_short=1000 is an ARBITRARY round amplitude, NOT a derived one: unlike VAD-GATE-002..006 it is not ceil(target * 32767) and corresponds to no target RMS. What matters is only that it is a fixture LITERAL, so a reverted production VAD_RMS_NORMALIZATION_DIVISOR cannot cancel out against a test-time derivation. Raw (unfiltered) normalized RMS is ~0.021566: comfortably above the default 0.005 threshold, but only ~7.8% above the tuned 0.02 threshold -- a modest margin, not a comfortable one. The 85 Hz Butterworth highpass attenuates 30 Hz to ~12% passthrough, so the production-seam filtered RMS is ~0.0027, BELOW threshold. WHAT THIS PINS: that the highpass is load-bearing for this verdict -- removing it, or reverting the RMS input to the unfiltered frame, flips expected_gate_open from false to true. WHAT IT DOES NOT PIN: the >= boundary (see VAD-GATE-002), or the normalization divisor (pinned by VadGateRmsFixtureTest, not by these vectors).

energy-floor gate at default silenceThreshold=0.005 -- nominally the 'at threshold' case, but see WHAT IT DOES NOT PIN below. Signal: a Nyquist-frequency square wave (raw i16 samples alternating +amplitude_short/-amplitude_short every sample). amplitude_short=164 is a LITERAL precomputed offline as ceil(0.005 * 32767) -- not derived from the production VAD_RMS_NORMALIZATION_DIVISOR at test time. A 2nd-order Butterworth highpass has EXACT unity gain at Nyquist, so the production-seam filtered RMS is ~0.00500504. WHAT THIS PINS: that a signal marginally above the threshold resolves to gate-open through the real filter+RMS path. WHAT IT DOES NOT PIN: the >= versus > semantics. ceil() places this vector STRICTLY ABOVE 0.005 (0.00500504, not equal to it), so flipping isEnergyAboveGate from >= to > leaves this vector and all five siblings green. The >= boundary is pinned by SilenceThresholdTest, not here.

energy-floor gate at default silenceThreshold=0.005 -- above threshold. Same Nyquist-square-wave construction as VAD-GATE-002; amplitude_short=197 is a LITERAL precomputed offline as ceil(0.006 * 32767).

WHAT THIS PINS: that a signal marginally above the tuned threshold resolves to gate-open through the real filter+RMS path. WHAT IT DOES NOT PIN: the >= versus > semantics. ceil() places this vector STRICTLY ABOVE 0.02 (0.02002014, not equal to it), so flipping isEnergyAboveGate from >= to > leaves it green. The >= boundary is pinned by SilenceThresholdTest, not here.

energy-floor gate at a tuned silenceThreshold=0.02 -- above threshold. Same Nyquist-square-wave construction as VAD-GATE-002; amplitude_short=689 is a LITERAL precomputed offline as ceil(0.021 * 32767).
stop-latency (frames-to-stop) at default silenceSecs=2.0 -- ceil(2.0 * 31.25) = 63 (AC6); above the AC2 7-frame floor
stop-latency at a tuned silenceSecs=0.5 -- ceil(0.5 * 31.25) = 16; still above the AC2 7-frame floor
stop-latency at a very small tuned silenceSecs=0.05 -- exercises the AC2 200ms-equivalent floor (ceil(0.05 * 31.25) = 2, floored up to 7)

The hangover TRIGGER EDGE, story 13-2 / B6 / D-L21. The VAD-LATENCY-* vectors above pin how many silent frames are REQUIRED (ceil(secs * 31.25), floored at 7); they say nothing about which frame actually fires, and both platforms passed them while disagreeing by one frame. PINS: with required_silent_frames = N consecutive non-speech frames after speech, the auto-stop edge has NOT fired at the N-th and HAS fired at the (N+1)-th. That is what Rust's advance_state has always done (Speaking -> Hangover{N} on the first non-speech frame, then one decrement per frame, Silence when frames_left <= 1, i.e. on frame N+1; its own test feeds 1+18+1 for N=19). Android fired at the N-th (`silentFrames >= requiredSilentFrames`) and auto-stopped ~32 ms early for the same configured silenceSecs. DOES NOT PIN: the 200 ms / 7-frame floor (VAD-LATENCY-003), the frames-per-second constant (VAD-LATENCY-001), or the repeatable live-preview pause counter, which keeps the one-frame difference on purpose -- audit row D-L21 cites only the auto-stop counter and ADR-0016:260 narrows B6 to the three measured deltas (see the story's Design Notes and frontmatter `deferred`).

Story 13-2 / B6 / D-L19, direction reversed by Andi 2026-09-21 (Desktop adapts to Android). PINS: on a frame whose RMS is BELOW the energy floor, (a) the speech predictor is still invoked exactly once with that frame, and (b) the energy gate still reports closed, so the frame is classified Silence. Silero is recurrent -- `predict(&mut self)` mutates the LSTM hidden state -- so skipping the call freezes the model's sliding window through every quiet passage and the frames AFTER the pause are scored from a stale state. Android has always called on every frame (KlarvoAudioRecorder.vadGateDecision); Desktop skipped (`if energy_ok { predict } else { 0.0 }`) and now does not. DOES NOT PIN: the resulting per-frame VERDICT changing -- it provably does not, because advance_state ANDs energy_ok into both thresholds; nor the probability the real model returns for silence (no Linux test can decide that); nor the CPU cost, which is recorded in the story rather than measured here.
